Inspect a pyramid set

Source: R/set.R
a5_pyramid_set_info.Rd

Reads the index of a set written by a5_write_pyramid_set(), set.json, without opening any shard. A renderer reads it first, then the footers of the shards its view meets.

Usage

a5_pyramid_set_info(src)

Arguments

src

The set's directory, or its set.json.

Value

A list of class a5pyramid_set_info:

  • path: the set's directory.

  • format_version, generator, a5_crate and a5_index, as in a5_pyramid_info().

  • data_resolution: the leaves' resolution.

  • bbox: c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) of every shard.

  • columns: a tibble of the value columns' name, type, reducer and sd, the standard deviation that scaled a "rep_child" column (1 where the leaves' standard deviation is 0 or undefined; NA for other reducers and older files).

  • tiers: a tibble with one row per tier: tier (from 0), lod_min, lod_max, shard_resolution, tile_size, and its shards, rows and bytes.

  • shards: a tibble with one row per shard: tier, cell (the shard cell, an a5R::a5_cell), path (relative to the set's directory), rows, tiles, bytes, footer_bytes (what a reader fetches to open it) and xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax.

  • metadata: the set's metadata, a named character vector.

See also

a5_pyramid_info() for one shard.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
dest <- tempfile()
a5_write_pyramid_set(data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells))), dest)
a5_pyramid_set_info(dest)$tiers
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>    tier lod_min lod_max shard_resolution tile_size shards  rows bytes
#>   <int>   <int>   <int>            <int>     <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     0       2      12                0     16384      2    46  6591
#> 2     1      13      15                3     16384      1  1380 11857
